subject: Plotting Python LAGRANGE output with BioGeoBEARS

messages.author: bcb2f3884a1e5527
messages.subject: Plotting Python LAGRANGE output with BioGeoBEARS
parts:
Dear users,

I just started using BioGeoBEARS, sorry if my question is trivial (my R skills are increasing but I am not an expert).

I have done a phyton Lagrange analysis and used the script posted by Nick in the group:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/plot$20lagrange/biogeobears/3lkoBRmyvok/73HXYlMRHt8J

That's working perfectly with my dataset.

My question: Is there a way to plot the different state probabilites at nodes in the pie chart instead largest+others, in the script: ("Python LAGRANGE state probabilities\n(P(best state), then all others)")? Is there any way to print labels for those colors within the pie chart?

Thanks!

Manuel.

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: Plotting Python LAGRANGE output with BioGeoBEARS
parts:
Hi Manuel,

Sorry it took a bit for me to get back to this.  I don't think I programmed a ready way to do a pie-chart of all of the states from a Lagrange output.  IIRC Lagrange just gives probabilities of the states/ranges that occupy the top 95% of the probability, not the probabilities of all of the states, so (1) they don't add up to 100% and (2) the states list will be different for each node, making the programming and coloring more complex.  It would be solvable, but -- it would be way easier to just run DEC in BioGeoBEARS and use those pie charts!

If you really wanted to do it anyway, you could take the table provided by e.g. LGpy_splits_fn_to_table, convert this to a table with the nodes in rows and the state probabilities in columns, and then plot pie charts on the tree yourself using the "pie" option in ape's plot.phylo -- this is basically what BioGeoBEARS is doing anyway.

Cheers!
Nick

Re: legend -- there is no ready-made legend for this function, but you could construct a legend either in e.g. powerpoint, or by modifying this script:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#legends
